## Taxonomic Classification Using GTDB-Tk

Following genome quality assessment with CheckM, the 17 selected genome bins with estimated completeness greater than 15% were classified using the Genome Taxonomy Database Toolkit (GTDB-Tk).

The purpose of this step was to identify the bacterial groups represented in the Black Band Disease (BBD) metagenome and investigate which microorganisms may contribute to the metabolic processes associated with the disease.

GTDB-Tk uses conserved marker genes and reference genomes to assign taxonomic classifications to metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs).

### Taxonomic Classification Results

GTDB-Tk produced a bacterial classification summary in `gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv`.

The family, genus and species classifications of the 17 selected genome bins are summarised below. Unresolved taxonomic ranks are omitted for clarity.


```{r taxonomy-summary, echo=TRUE}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)

gtdbtk <- read.delim(
  "gtdbtk/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv"
)

taxonomy_summary <- gtdbtk %>%
  select(user_genome, classification) %>%
  separate_longer_delim(classification, delim = ";") %>%
  group_by(user_genome) %>%
  slice_tail(n = 3) %>%
  filter(!classification %in% c("f__", "g__", "s__")) %>%
  mutate(
    classification = sub("^f__", "Family: ", classification),
    classification = sub("^g__", "Genus: ", classification),
    classification = sub("^s__", "Species: ", classification)
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    short_classification = paste(classification, collapse = "; "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(user_genome)

kable(
  taxonomy_summary,
  col.names = c("Genome bin", "Taxonomic classification"),
  caption = "GTDB-Tk classifications of the selected genome bins"
)

```


The classification of `metabat.40` as *Roseofilum* is particularly relevant because this genus includes filamentous cyanobacteria associated with coral Black Band Disease.

The presence of this cyanobacterial genome is consistent with the expected microbial composition of BBD lesions, where photosynthetic microorganisms form an important component of the microbial community.

The bin `metabat.21` was classified within the family Vallitaleaceae, while `metabat.69` was classified as *Halarcobacter* within the family Arcobacteraceae.

These classifications provide a taxonomic basis for interpreting the metabolic pathways identified during subsequent functional analysis.

### Interpretation

The GTDB-Tk results demonstrate that the selected genome bins represent different bacterial lineages within the BBD microbial community.

In particular, the identification of *Roseofilum* provides a useful link between the taxonomic composition of the metagenome and the potential for photosynthesis.

However, taxonomic classification alone cannot confirm which metabolic processes are occurring. Functional gene annotation and pathway inference are needed to investigate the metabolic capabilities of these microorganisms.

Furthermore, many of the selected genome bins have relatively low estimated completeness, which may limit the resolution of their taxonomic classifications.

### Processing Log

The 17 selected genome bins were copied from the MetaBAT2 output directory into the GTDB-Tk input directory.

```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/gtdbtk

while read bin;do
  cp "../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa" genomes
done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```

This loop used the bin identifiers stored in `bbd_topbins.txt` to copy the corresponding FASTA files into `gtdbtk/genomes/`.

The copied files were checked using:

```{bash}
ls genomes
```

GTDB-Tk was then run through the SLURM scheduler using the script [run_gtdbtk.sh](gtdbtk/run_gtdbtk.sh).

The main classification command was:

```{bash}
gtdbtk classify_wf -x fa --cpus 2 --genome_dir genomes --out_dir out --skip_ani_screen
```

The `classify_wf` option performed the taxonomic classification workflow, `-x fa` specified the FASTA extension, `--cpus 2` allocated two processing threads, and `--genome_dir` and `--out_dir` specified the input and output directories.

The job was submitted using:

```{bash}
sbatch run_gtdbtk.sh
```

After completion, the classification summary was checked and copied into the main GTDB-Tk directory so it could be included in the GitHub repository.

```{bash}
ls -l out/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv

cp out/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv .
```

The taxonomic classifications were subsequently cross-referenced with the metabolic pathway results generated by MinPath.
